findings.claim: G-d gave him the Torah, including the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:2–14).
findings.issue: The Ten Commandments span Exodus 20:2–17, not 20:2–14. Verse 14 is only the seventh commandment (do not commit adultery). The commandments against stealing (v.15), false witness (v.16), and coveting (v.17) fall outside the cited range. Any student who looks up the reference will find it stops mid-Decalogue.
findings.correction: The correct citation is Exodus 20:2–17 (or Exodus 20:1–17). The Decalogue ends at verse 17.

findings.claim: Every synagogue contains five essential features: the Ark (Aron Kodesh) housing the Torah scrolls; the Bimah (raised reading platform); the Ner Tamid (Eternal Light); the Sefer Torah (handwritten Torah scroll); and the Mikveh (ritual immersion pool) nearby for purification.
findings.issue: The mikveh is not a feature of the synagogue building itself, and is not universally present on synagogue premises. Standard GCSE OCR teaching — and Jewish practice — identifies four essential interior synagogue features: Ark, Bimah, Ner Tamid, and Sefer Torah. The mikveh is a separate communal facility that may be nearby or in a separate building. Listing it as a fifth 'essential feature' of every synagogue is factually incorrect and would mislead students answering exam questions on synagogue features.
findings.correction: Remove the mikveh from the list of essential synagogue features. The four essential features of every synagogue are: the Ark (Aron Kodesh), the Bimah, the Ner Tamid, and the Sefer Torah. A brief note can mention that communities maintain a mikveh as a separate communal facility, but it is not part of the synagogue's interior features.

findings.claim: wine is blessed and then spilled to extinguish the flame
findings.issue: The Havdalah wine is not 'spilled' to extinguish the flame as the primary ritual action. The correct sequence is: the wine blessing is recited, most of the wine is drunk, and then the remaining drops are used to douse the candle flame (either by dipping the candle into leftover wine in a tray, or pouring the residue over it). The wine is chiefly consumed, not spilled. Describing it as 'wine is blessed and then spilled' reverses the order and mischaracterises the ritual.
findings.correction: After reciting the blessing, the wine is drunk (most of it). The candle is then extinguished in the remaining drops of wine that are poured into a dish, or by dipping the candle into them. Example wording: 'The blessing is recited over wine, the wine is drunk, spices are smelled, and the braided candle is extinguished in the remaining drops of wine.'
